title: Does Model Size Modulate Homogeneity? Comparing 7B, 13B, 70B, and Frontier Model Homogeneity Profiles

original_idea.title: Does Model Size Modulate Homogeneity? Comparing 7B, 13B, 70B, and Frontier Model Homogeneity Profiles
original_idea.problem: The Artificial Hivemind paper aggregated across model sizes. It is unknown whether smaller or larger models contribute more to inter-model homogeneity.
original_idea.direction: Stratify the existing Infinity-Chat experimental setup by model parameter count and compare intra-size-class vs. cross-size-class homogeneity.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If frontier models are the most homogeneous, the concentration of deployment in this tier amplifies systemic risk; if smaller models are more diverse, this has implications for deployment portfolio design.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind tested 70+ models but did not report size-stratified analysis; the Infinity-Chat benchmark supports this analysis directly.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: understanding the size-homogeneity relationship is informative for deployment strategy, but the direct chain to safety improvement is unclear.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: stratifying existing data by model size and computing similarity metrics is manageable for CS students with data analysis skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: size-stratified homogeneity analysis using existing Infinity-Chat data, with clear intra-class vs. cross-class comparison.

novelty.reasoning: The Artificial Hivemind paper aggregated across model sizes and did not report size-stratified analysis. Scaling laws literature focuses on performance, not inter-model similarity. This is a natural disaggregation of the Hivemind findings that no one has published, and the Infinity-Chat data potentially supports it directly.

evidence.finding: Tested 70+ models but did not report size-stratified analysis of homogeneity.
Extensive work on how model size affects performance, but not on how it affects inter-model homogeneity.
